Only what is listed here is accepted. An unapproved algorithm, an absent one,
or an unparseable one is a REJECTION, not a business answer — the same
What makes this enforceable: oid4vc-service reports the algorithms it
observed on each presentation in /vp/status as `algs` (fork commit 1583b7bd).
`alg` lives in a JWS protected header and never reaches the claim set, so
before that change a relying party could not see it, and Iteration 01
recorded the allowlist as a deviation rather than shipping a control that
did nothing. That reporting exists now, so the control is real.
ES256 because that is what identity-service signs SD-JWT VCs with and what
Paradym's holder keys use. EdDSA (Ed25519) because credentials-service signs
ldp_vc credentials with Ed25519Signature2020, which oid4vc-service reports as
EdDSA, and Inji-based wallets may bind with Ed25519 keys. Both are current,
strong signature algorithms. Widening this list further is a security
decision and belongs in review, which is why it is a version-controlled file
